body: Why forcing us to have a `results` property set to `undefined` ?

So you decided to spread the previous render state to follow `getWidgetUiState` current implementation.

Anything against migrating `getWidgetUiState` so we do not have to spread the previous state in any of them? (see discussion on Slack: https://algolia.slack.com/archives/C1T50SYEN/p1595847932000300 )

I know we agreed on spreading for consistency, but now it seems a little odd to me. I wonder if we could have the key being calculated based on the $$type and return directly the object containing query? Not sure yet what's better, but this seems quite indirect
The reason I'm thinking this, is because the hook is get**Widget**RenderState, not `getCurrentRenderState`
interesting that connectSearchBox didn't forward them, but I think the other methods call renderFn with searchMeta, helper, results, state...
should we call render with uiState too? Seems simpler

> I wonder if we could have the key being calculated based on the $$type

That's what I was thinking initially but in the end it's way more shady. That's an implicit API.

> The reason I'm thinking this, is because the hook is get**Widget**RenderState, not `getCurrentRenderState`

We've got the same behavior for `getWidgetUiState` which returns the whole index UI state, not the widget UI state.
Nope, very few connectors call `renderFn` with all these information.

I didn't because we made the mistake to call this `uiState` instead of `initialUiState`, which would be extremely misleading when passed to `render()`. You would expect this `uiState` to be up-to-date.
I feel like this iteration on all renderFn is a moment to standardise that, wdyt?
You're right, I forgot this was only initial
Perhaps as a last set of PRs in the "Render State" scope, but let's not introduce too many changes right now.
So that we have close to argument-parity in `init` and `render`. Do you think that's too explicit? (note that this is internal code)

I didn't want to rush that decision now because it might be too naive. There are probably things that we'll miss. E.g., inability for a widget to be responsible of multiple UI states—that could be the case if `infiniteHits` starts controlling another UI state than `page`. Besides, that'd be a breaking change.
Is it normal to do it on `localWidgets` while we execute the `init` method only on `widgets` just after ?
You can merge this loop with the following one.
I think it would be better to have it as a method in `index`, it would simplify the signature (no need to pass `instantSearchInstance` and `parent`).
Yeah I don't really see any advantage in doing that, I find it confusing for the reader.
The point of the discussion was that if we do the merge ourself it would not be a breaking change and it should not have any impact on the widgets that return a full UI State in all cases.
To my first point, I don't think this is the right time to do this, and we'll need proper testing to decide if we want to do this at some point.
Good catch.
Nope, otherwise we won't get the full render state passed to the widget when they `render`. The goal of having this as a loop before rendering is to do a full pass to construct the render state.

The params values are not the same during `init` and `render` so we cannot share them between these two methods.

Reusing the same params between `getWidgetRenderState` and `init|render` might leads to bug because they could expose stale values.
We call it only twice (and will call it only one time once when remove the `init` method). Besides, it would make it available on the `index` widget scope, which we want to avoid.
Ok, since this particularity is not explicit in the code could you add a comment to explain it?

Not sharing between `init` and `render` but between `getWidgetRenderState`/`init` and then `getWidgetRenderState`/`render`.

For the stale value problem, the 2 calls are synchronous and the only thing that is updated between them is `renderState`, it could be passed separately from the option object to avoid that.
If you do not want to expose it you can set it as a "private" function, like `createURL`.
It feels like a missed opportunity here but ok.
There's a lot of properties going on in that function call, but I think similar code "twice" is still okay.
